reviews.comment: Awful lectures, reads off the board the entire time using a laser pointer with his back turned most of the time. Exams are multiple choice with 5 choices and he does not give ANY partial credit. He also tells you there will be 10 quizes, 1 per week, but will forget half the time, or even end up doing multiple per week so you cannot really know...

Dropped because I'm only taking the class for a minor I can't complete due to scheduling conflicts. The physics in this class is extremely easy, but Dr. Fry doesn't do a great job of teaching. Physics is math and derivation heavy, but he just has text on slides that he reads off in a monotone voice. Also not great at helping confused students.

Professor Fry is probably the worst professor at Texas A&M. He prepares his slides in advance, just reads off of them, and expects everyone to understand. He only used a marker and board to explain physics when there was a misprint on the exam. The homework does not reflect the test questions. He is barely audible in class; do not take Fry.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are very fast-paced, but that is in part due to how much content there is. Dr. Fry is very kind and accessible outside of class. My advice would be to make sure you stop him in class if there is something you don't understand,  go to his office hours if you still have trouble, and make sure you understand and do the homework + other probs

This class is not easy, but Fry is a caring professor and you can tell he wants his students to do well. He's really old so lectures can be disorganized, but the homeworks and the questions he gives out will prepare you well for the test. He's very accessible over email and in his office and heavily curves. Tests are 75%, quizzes 7%, HW 18%.

Fry is a nice guy, but a terrible professor. His homework is long and tedious and often pertains to subjects later in the course, his lectures are boring and tangential (and his voice is way too quiet), there's a pop quiz almost every week, and the tests are abysmal. One of the most difficult classes I had to endure.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His Homeworks are long, tedious, and useless. Lectures are just him reading off 100 equations. He drops quizzes on you (20% of your grade) with one minute to complete them. He is a very tough grader. The tests are long he sets the average at 60. Personally, I've never understood the point of making sure that most of the class fails but whatever.

No feedback. Must attend office hours. Go to Tutor John and you will get an A or B in this class. Tests weigh a lot. You must go to tutoring for it. Do not take if pre-professional school. This class is difficult.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Physics at TAMU is just insanely hard for no reason. If you dod the practice tests they are nothing like the actual exams. Fry is a good professor but just makes tests way too hard. Take phys at a community college because TAMU is not it.

His lectures are absolutely atrocious. He reads off the PowerPoint slides in a monotone voice and expects the students to absorb everything he says. He's an absolute angel of a man and genuinely cares about his students' success but he is quite simply too outdated in his delivery and interaction with students. Use tutor john or do the hw 20 times.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great guy, not so good professor. I worked my butt off to get an A in this class. I taught myself the material from the mastering physics and online videos. There is a ridiculous amount of online homework as well. Expect to spend 4-5 hours on homework unless you chegg the whole thing. Stopped attending lecture about half way through the semester.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Fry is a very sweet man and loves physics, but should not be teaching. His lectures are useless as he just reads off slides and does not teach to his tests. The test averages were terrible although he does give a generous curve. I taught myself the whole course. This was not worth the stress, please find another professor.

He's a nice guy, but totally oblivious. His lectures are extremely boring and aren't beneficial. Homework is nothing like the tests. Rampant cheating on his exams because he proctors his own exams of 200+ students. Exam averages are extremely bad and curves didn't make much sense, but were generous.

Super sweet guy and probably physics' number one fan, but not a good prof. His lectures don't actually explain anything, they just throw formulas your way. I studied for at least eight hours before every exam and got Cs or Ds, even with the VERY GENEROUS curve. Did all the homework, read the book, and watched tons of videos but it wasn't enough.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's a great guy, but he's not a great lecturer. He can be really hard to follow in class. He really cares about his students, but since we're supposed to rate mainly based off of teaching and not personality, that's why the numbers I submit are so extreme. If you take his class, the homework is not enough. You have to work other book problems.

Dr. Fry, while a nice guy, is not a great professor. It's clear that he's been teaching this class for so long that it's kind of just an old routine for him. Lots of mastering physics homework, lectures by literally reading (sometimes wrong) powerpoint slides to the class. It's not hard to get an A if you put in some effort, but you won't like it.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: He's a great guy, very nice and all but his lectures are poor. The slides are full with too many equations and he flies through them so you really just have to sit and listen. I have to read the book and go over the slides again to understand the material. Homework problems take forever and are not very helpful for tests. Exams were pretty fair

I absolutely loved Dr. Fry, one of my favorite professors, potentially my favorite professor so far. He is one of the nicest people I've ever met. Has very clear lectures where he does an amazing job explaining the physics. He reminded me a bit of a grandpa but in the best way and I'll really miss this class a lot.

Fry's Exams were tough. Made a 20 on my first exam. Good thing is he drops the lowest exam grade (final not included) and three of the lowest quiz grades. The exams are hard to study for but he does however let you have an equation sheet for the exams, which makes it easier. But overall a very, very tough class.
